.NEAR TERM...
(Tonight)
Issued at 231 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

Tranquil weather across the Tennessee Valley this afternoon with
high pressure promoting clear/sunny conditions. Other than a few
bands of cirrus moving in overnight, the mostly clear sky will
continue and subsequently there will be a good setup for
radiational cooling in this dry air mass. Still given the warmer
conditions today and some light, persistent easterly winds, 
temperatures will run a few degrees higher tonight -- as overnight 
low temperatures will fall into the low to mid 40s in most
locations.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Thursday through Saturday)
Issued at 906 AM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

The aforementioned pattern of sfc high pressure will continue to
allow dry conditions for the Tennessee Valley as the area remains
between two low pressure systems- one shifting northeast into the
Great Lakes region and one looming over Florida. A slight warming
trend is in store as high temperatures reach the upper 60s to lower
70s in most of the area throughout the short term. Overnight lows
during this time are forecast to drop into the upper 40s to mid
50s.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Friday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 1054 PM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

Upper ridging will largely dominate the eastern CONUS to start the 
weekend; however, a cutoff low further develops off the east coast of
Florida and slowly makes its way northeast through early next week. 
Meanwhile, a shortwave trough looks to traverse the Mississippi 
River Valley but weaken as it progresses farther east over the 
Tennessee Valley Sunday night into Monday. Upper ridging will then 
take hold Monday into Tuesday. At the surface, high pressure over the
eastern US will be pushed east through the weekend as a cold front 
sweeps over the Mississippi River Valley. This feature is then shown
to move over the region Sunday into Monday, with high pressure 
pushing southward from Canada by Tuesday. 

Overall, the weather pattern stays fairly dry. The main time window 
of any precipitation potential is Sunday into Monday with frontal 
passage. However, the question will be whether enough moisture 
remains/is realized with FROPA for showers to occur. This will be 
monitored. As for temperatures, expect highs in the upper 60s to 
lower 70s on Saturday to drop into the mid 50s to lower 60s by 
Tuesday. Lows will follow a similar pattern, beginning in the mid 40s
to lower 50s Friday night and dropping into the 30s once again by 
Monday night.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 544 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

VFR conditions will prevail through the TAF period. Easterly 
winds around 5 knots or so tonight will shift to be more 
southeasterly and increase to around 10 knots through Thursday 
morning. Light easterly winds are then forecast to develop by late
Thursday afternoon and into the evening.
